newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - Market comments on British election.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Market comments on British election.

text.p: The following is a selection of analysts' reactions to Britain's May 1 election, where the opposition Labour party is sweeping towards a landslide victory.
DAVID DEAKIN, TREASURER, BANK OF BERMUDA

0125 GMT - "While a large majority was expected, personally I'm surprised at the size of it. The effect of it has taken a bit of the edge off sterling. Such a strong move to what was a socialist party might well frighten the market, but it is a result, which is never a bad thing in the eyes of the market.

"We have up to two months to wait for a budget and we'll probably be on hold until then. It would be quite useful to sterling were Gordon Brown to make a prompt move on interest rates, which I think he will do. It would show his commitment to low inflation and the market would like that."
RICHARD HILL, HEAD OF FX TRADING AT BANK OF AMERICA
0025 GMT - "There are some worries that this is giving the Labour Party carte blanche to do what they want to do."
GERARD LYONS, CHIEF ECONOMIST, DKB INTERNATIONAL
0020 GMT - "Having clearly won over the floating voters, Labour's immediate task will be to win the confidence of the financial markets.

"There won't be any dramatic shift in policy, just an endorsement of the tough fiscal stance and a commitment to tackle inflation by raising interest rates. I think they'll do that next week at the monetary policy meeting...but I still don't think rates will go up as much as the market is expecting. I think rates will go up in two quarter point moves.
"I think the pound's going to remain strong. I don't think gilts will do a lot initially... but yields will trend down as inflation remains low."
